title: The Inconsistency Introduced by i:  Why Quantum Mechanics Cannot Bring Itself Back
description: Quantum mechanics treats energy and phase as already-existing wholes, then divides them formally. That is the wrong algebraic structure for a physical process in which the whole only exists after the phase closes. Therefore, QM is not truly algebraically unitary. The correct algebra for a physical process is not one that assumes the existence of divisible wholes, but one where wholes emerge through phase instantiation. The i in Schrödinger’s equation encodes an ontology of reversible division that no physical process can sustain.
